19.t: Working with data: hormones in one cycle
q: Identify the day of ovulation, with evidence from the graph.
Day 14: the LH surge (peak of 40), just after the oestradiol peak.
Explain how rising oestradiol before day 13 leads to the LH surge.
High oestradiol has a positive feedback effect on the pituitary, which releases a large burst of LH (and some FSH).
Explain why progesterone is high from day 16 to day 24.
After ovulation the follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone to keep the endometrium thick.
Explain why FSH and LH stay low from day 16 to day 24.
Progesterone and oestradiol have a negative feedback effect on the hypothalamus and pituitary, so no new follicles develop.
Predict progesterone after day 24 if an embryo had implanted. Explain.
It would stay high: the embryo releases hCG, which keeps the corpus luteum alive, so the endometrium is kept and there is no menstruation.
